stem: Which one of the following is used in the manufacture of soaps?
expl: Soap is a combination of animal fat or plant oil and caustic soda. When dissolved in water, it breaks dirt away from the surface. The modern soap makers use the fat that has been processed into fatty acids. This eliminates many impurities and it produces water as a by-product instead of glycerine. Many vegetable fats including olive oil, palm kernel oil and coconut oil are also used in soap making.

expl: Emulsifiers are usually long chain compounds with polar groups for example-soap. The soap molecules consist of two parts- (i) long hydrocarbon chain (C H ) which is soluble in fat and (ii) dissolved polar parts in water (COO– Na+). During emulsion, the dipolar alkaline group of soap dissolves oil or grease and the polar group get dissolved in water. When rubbed, the greases are suspended in the water in the form of small droplets and flows smoothly with water.

A detergent is different from soap. A detergent is a surfactant or a mixture of surfactants with cleaning and refining properties in dilute solutions. The most important ingredients in detergents are chemicals called surfactants. The term detergent by itself refers specifically to laundry detergent or dish detergent as opposed to hand soap or other types of cleaning agents. Detergents are commonly available as a powder or concentrated solutions.

stem: Detergents used for cleaning clothes are :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Detergents used for cleaning clothes are usually alkylbenzene sulfonates, a family of compounds that are similar to soap but are more soluble in hard water.

stem:
Assertion (A) : Detergent easily removes oil and dirt from dirty garments.
Reason (R) : Detergent increases the surface tension of water.
Code :

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: Assertion (A) is true as the detergent easily removes oil and dirt from dirty garments. The surface tension of water is dramatically reduced by the addition of soap or detergent. The soap or detergent molecules tend to aggregate at the surface of the water. By this, they weaken the hydrogen bonding between water molecules, hence, surface tension reduces. Hence (A) is true, but (R) is false.

stem:
Assertion (A) : Synthetic detergents can make more lather in hard water.
Reason (R) : Synthetic detergents form soluble calcium and magnesium salts with hard water.

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: Detergents are different from soap. They are used to clean clothes with hard water as detergent does not form any insoluble precipitate with calcium and magnesium salts. They form water-soluble calcium and magnesium salts. This is the reason why detergents produce more foam with hard water and remove oil and dust from dirty clothes.

stem:
Consider the following statements : Sodium silicate and sodium sulphate are mixed as detergents in washing powders so that–
1. To maintain dryness of the powder.
2. To maintain the basicity of powder.
Which of the following statement is correct?
expl: By adding sodium sulphate to the washing powder, it increases the basicity of the powder. The addition of sodium silicate into the washing powder turns the powder crystalline, so that the powder stays in dry form.
